input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 20 claims (independent device claim 1, system claim 11, method claim 16, and dependent claims 2-10, 12-15, 17-20), all 17 numerals in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48), every numbered part and relationship in the Field, Summary, Brief Description and Detailed Description, and all six figure briefs (FIG. 1 perspective, FIG. 2 section on 2-2, FIG. 3 bottom plan, FIG. 4 enlarged section on 4-4, FIG. 5 pulling element, FIG. 6 stirring elements) were traced to affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and to the single technical USER passage in input/conversation.md ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"), which supports the autonomous embodiment, claim 10, the FIG. 6 brief and the "autonomously moving" clause of the Field. Rigid base, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism such as a vacuum pump on the first side in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, the rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter of the second side (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations of rigid materials), the non-sealing restriction of inflow, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, the pressure-differential hold without operator downforce, the rigid undamped transmission path, free sliding across areas of the tile with the hold never released, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control all trace to exact disclosure sentences. The bearing face 26, clearance 34, exposed face 38, bonding material 40 and substrate 42 trace to "air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", "not intended to form a complete airtight seal", "maintaining rigid contact with the tile", "setting tiles ... into thinset, mortar, adhesive" and "the bond between the tile and the underlying substrate". Depiction conventions were audited against the functional-surface rule: the flat lower end of the column in FIG. 4 (bearing face shape disclaimed), the schematic gap through the slab in FIG. 2 (no port, duct or valve construction asserted), the ring width and angular section-line positions in FIG. 3, the three-block placement and handle mounting in FIG. 1, the schematic cord attachment in FIG. 5, and the number, form and carriage position of the stirring elements in FIG. 6 are each confined to their figure briefs, are marked schematic, and are matched by shape-neutral, location-neutral claim and description text; none verbalizes an undisclosed taper, angle, runout, depth ordering, circumferential position or contact topology, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening was found in the application text or the Brief Description. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 repeat identically in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view headers, and draft/07-drawings.md; every numeral in each brief's list is defined in the numeral table and appears in the description; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person or unresolved alternative remains in any section body. Background prior-art characterizations were not treated as requiring inventor support and citation tracing is left to the later independent review. One verified defect was found: a single terminology slip in the Detailed Description that names numbered part 10 as "the vibrating device" instead of "the vibration device 10". No unsupported technical assertion was found.

findings.title: Numbered part 10 is named "the vibrating device" in one sentence, breaking the single-designation rule
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, force-balance paragraph in the section "The vibration transmission path"
findings.detail: Throughout the specification, claims and figure briefs, reference numeral 10 is designated "the vibration device" (numeral table: "10 | vibration device"; description: "The vibration device 10 comprises a base 12, a vibration motor 18, an air-extraction mechanism 20 and a perimeter member 24"). In one sentence of the force-balance paragraph the same part is instead called "the vibrating device", without its reference numeral. That introduces a second designation for a numbered part and leaves the phrase without antecedent basis in the description, contrary to the opening recital that "the same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout the drawings". This is a wording inconsistency only; the technical substance of the sentence (no downward force from the operator, so no loaded path into the hands, wrists, arms and joints) is supported by the disclosure: "The resulting pressure differential holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward" and "This transfers vibration into the operator's hands, wrists, arms, and joints".
findings.evidence: Candidate wording: "Because no downward force is required from the operator, no loaded path need be maintained from the vibrating device into the operator's hands, wrists, arms and joints." Compare the immediately preceding sentence in the same paragraph: "the force the operator need supply is an in-plane force sufficient to overcome that frictional resistance and to steer", and the surrounding usage "The force balance on the vibration device 10 in use is as follows."
findings.fix: Replace "the vibrating device" with "the vibration device 10" so the sentence reads: "Because no downward force is required from the operator, no loaded path need be maintained from the vibration device 10 into the operator's hands, wrists, arms and joints." No other text changes.
